done_state: tessera/common/ provides canonical_json(), sha256_hex(), event_hash(), and utc_now_iso() with no third-party dependencies, importable and passing their own test suite standalone.

criteria.statement: canonical_json(obj) is deterministic regardless of input dict key order.
canonical_json(obj) raises TypeError on a non-JSON-serializable value rather than silently dropping or coercing it.
sha256_hex(data) matches Python stdlib hashlib.sha256 on known test vectors, including empty input and unicode input.
event_hash(payload) = sha256_hex(canonical_json(payload)) composition is stable: two dicts with the same content in different key order produce the identical event_hash.
utc_now_iso() returns an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp string parseable by datetime.fromisoformat after normalizing a trailing 'Z', and successive calls are non-decreasing.
tessera/common/ imports only Python stdlib modules, no third-party packages.
criteria.verification: python3 tessera/common/tests/check_stdlib_only.py exits 0 (parses every import in tessera/common/*.py, excluding tests/, and asserts each resolves to a stdlib module).

failure_criteria.statement: canonical_json or event_hash fails open on bad input (returns a value instead of raising) on the path that matters for hash integrity.
failure_criteria.detection: C2 explicitly asserts a rejection path exists, not only an acceptance path.

failure_criteria.statement: A numeric claim about hashing/timestamp behavior appears in a docstring with no reproduction path.
failure_criteria.detection: grep the diff for numeric claims; each must name the command that produced it.

failure_criteria.statement: Code assumes a locale, timezone, or platform-specific float/str repr that isn't actually pinned.
failure_criteria.detection: test_event_hash_stable_across_key_order and test_sha256_hex_vectors run against fixed, explicit inputs, not environment-derived values.

failure_criteria.statement: An error in canonical_json/sha256_hex/utc_now_iso is written to a channel nobody reads.
failure_criteria.detection: No function in this component catches and logs-only; every error path is either a return value or a raised exception a caller must handle.

out_of_scope: Encryption or signing of any kind.
Timestamp formats other than ISO 8601 UTC.
Any store/api/gitops/reviewui-specific logic — this component is generic utilities only.
constraints: Python 3.9+ stdlib only (hashlib, json, datetime) — no third-party dependencies.
Must be importable standalone without importing any other tessera component (store, api, gitops, reviewui must not be imported from here, to avoid a dependency cycle back through common).

results.evidence:
$ /usr/bin/python3 tessera/common/tests/check_stdlib_only.py
OK: tessera/common imports only stdlib
